title: RunProducts
description: What a run wrote under its work/ directory, as the daemon finds it when a client asks for the view ProductsOfRun: one row per run the daemon knows. The daemon reads the directory from the host through one reader (runbook/src/engine/products.rs) with the guards of the inspector's file route: no link is followed or listed, a file with more than one name is not listed, a name that starts with a dot is neither listed nor entered, and the walk stops at 500 files, 2000 directories, 20000 entries and 6 levels. The language cannot read a file system, so no command creates or changes a row, as with Runbook.

run_id.description: The run whose work/ directory this is.

cut.description: The bound the listing stopped at: files, directories, entries or depth; absent when it walked the whole directory.

hidden.description: Entries whose name starts with a dot: neither listed nor served.

left_out.description: Links and files with more than one name: neither listed nor served.

sdc.daemon.ProductFile.title: ProductFile
sdc.daemon.ProductFile.description: One file of a run's work/ directory as the listing names it: a regular file with one name, reached through no link.

sdc.daemon.ProductPath.title: ProductPath
sdc.daemon.ProductPath.description: The path of a file of a run, relative to the run's work/ directory (its workspace, which the cases of the run share): names joined by `/`, none of them `..` and none starting with a dot. Never absolute and never a path of the host.

sdc.daemon.RunId.title: RunId
sdc.daemon.RunId.description: The id of a run. The daemon mints it (a UUID, version 7) in the HTTP handler and returns it in the answer to the submit; the handler fills the `run_id` input of SubmitRun and a client never chooses it. The state directory of the run is named after it. A run id that is already taken cannot occur, because the daemon mints it; the specification has no refusal for it.

sdc.daemon.WorkId.title: WorkId
sdc.daemon.WorkId.description: The work/ directory of a run as a row of RunProducts: its text is the run's id. A type of its own, not RunId, because a row of that view is the listing of a directory and not the run.
